title: Pronouns: the full picture
topic: order of double pronouns; pronouns with the imperative; overall review
why: This lesson completes the pronoun unit with the order of double pronouns (je te le, je le lui, il y en a) and their place with every tense and with the imperative. It's a full review of direct, indirect and reflexive pronouns, y and en, through the preparation of a surprise party.

{"lessons": ["

Two pronouns in a row: the order

You now know all the object pronouns. Sometimes a sentence needs two of them: \"I'm giving it to you\". English puts them after the verb; French puts both before the verb, in a fixed order.

12345
me, te, se, nous, vousle, la, leslui, leuryen
Tu me prêtes ton livre ? — Oui, je te le prête.Will you lend me your book? — Yes, I'll lend it to you.
Je donne la clé à Paul. → Je la lui donne.I'm giving the key to Paul. → I'm giving it to him.
Il y a des gâteaux ? — Oui, il y en a.Are there any cakes? — Yes, there are some.
Tu as parlé du projet à Marie ? — Oui, je lui en ai parlé.Did you tell Marie about the project? — Yes, I told her about it.

Three rules of thumb

  • me, te, nous, vous come before le, la, les: Il nous les montre.
  • But le, la, les come before lui, leur: Je le leur envoie.
  • y and en always come last, and en is the very last: Je vous en donne.

In practice, you'll mostly meet a few combinations, so learn them as sounds: je te le, je le lui, je lui en, il y en a.

Lui and leur never go together with me, te, nous, vous before the verb. And le lui is correct, while « lui le » never is.

", "

Two pronouns with every tense

The order never changes. Only the position depends on the tense, exactly as with a single pronoun. In the table, les stands for les photos (feminine plural) and te for the person you're showing them to.

TenseWhere the pronouns goExample
presentbefore the verbJe te les montre.
passé composébefore the auxiliaryJe te les ai montrées.
near futurebefore the infinitiveJe vais te les montrer.
with pouvoir, vouloir…before the infinitiveJe peux te les montrer.

In the negative, ne comes before the whole block, and pas after the conjugated verb:

Je ne te le prête pas.I'm not lending it to you.
Je ne le lui ai pas dit.I didn't tell him (it).
Je ne vais pas le leur dire.I'm not going to tell them (it).

Agreement still applies

In the passé composé, the participle agrees with the direct object le, la, les placed before avoir, even with a second pronoun in between:

Les photos ? Je te les ai envoyées hier.The photos? I sent them to you yesterday.
La lettre ? Je la leur ai écrite.The letter? I wrote it to them.

Still no agreement with en: Des fleurs ? Je lui en ai offert.

Translating \"I told him\" or \"I told her\" about a fact: French often adds le: Je le lui ai dit (I told him so). Without it, the sentence sounds incomplete.

", "

Pronouns with the imperative

In an affirmative command, the pronouns follow the verb, joined by hyphens, and the order is simpler: direct before indirect, and me, te become moi, toi.

AffirmativeNegativeEnglish
Donne-le-moi !Ne me le donne pas !Give it to me! / Don't give it to me!
Envoie-la-leur !Ne la leur envoie pas !Send it to them! / Don't send it to them!
Rends-les-lui !Ne les lui rends pas !Give them back to him! / Don't give them back to him!
Dites-le-nous !Ne nous le dites pas !Tell us! / Don't tell us!

In the negative, everything goes back to the normal order and position: ne + pronouns + verb + pas.

With y and en

Before y and en, the tu form of -er verbs gets its -s back, for the liaison: Vas-y !, Manges-en ! (Eat some!). Just recognize forms like Parle-lui-en (Talk to him about it): they are rare in conversation.

The chain-replacement method

To build a sentence with two pronouns, replace one noun at a time:

J'offre les fleurs à Camille. → Je les offre à Camille. → Je les lui offre.I'm giving the flowers to Camille. → I'm giving them to Camille. → I'm giving them to her.

When you're not sure in conversation, one pronoun is fine: Je lui offre les fleurs is perfectly correct. Double pronouns make you sound fluent, but you can build up to them.
